rows.text: scans the dwords from `022CB9DC` through `022CB9E4` inclusive (three dwords, 4-byte step) and returns 1 at the first non-zero one, or 0 when all are 0

when `ecx` is -1, reads the bytes at absolute addresses 1 and 2 (a null base) and returns the sign-extended byte 1, plus 2 when byte 2 is non-zero; otherwise takes the `0x18`-byte entry `ecx AND 0xF` of the table at `022D9AE0` when `cl AND 0xF0` is non-zero, or of the table at `022D9AB0` when it is 0, and returns its sign-extended byte `+1`, plus 2 when its byte `+2` is non-zero

when `ecx` is 0 tail-jumps through the jump at `003A0E80` + 0x19 with `edx` as the first argument; when `ecx` is 1 tail-jumps through the jump at `003A0E80` + 0x11 with `edx` and 0; any other `ecx` returns without a call
returns bit 30 of `ecx` inverted: 1 when the bit is clear, 0 when it is set

returns 0 when byte `02B59D71` is non-zero; otherwise scans the 32 `0x150`-byte entries at `02B59D80` and, at the first whose word `+0` is non-zero and dword `+4` equals `ecx`, returns its dword `+0xC0 + edx*4` (`edx` zero-extended); returns 0 when none matches

notes: 0036EC50: the `ecx == -1` path sets `rdx` to 0 and reads `[rdx+1]`/`[rdx+2]`, so as listed it dereferences a null base; stated literally. 00360670: the loop bound uses `jle` (signed) on pointers; with these addresses it covers exactly three dwords. 003A0E80: on the fall-through path `eax` is not set by the body.
